title: feat(spec,service-automation,lint)!: an http node's url and headers are text slots, its body a value slot, the rest literals — the {…} token refused (#19939 pass 4, S5)
body:
Part of #19939
Clause-②: yes (narrowing: a {…} token is refused at http url, each headers value, any string of a literal body, method, durable, timeoutMs and signingSecret, and as a whole headers map, and a body value that names a dialect must be a valid CEL value envelope; widening: the exported FlowNodeTextSlot type gains the optional eachValue field, LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS gains http, and the published HttpConfig JSON Schema marks body as a value slot)

Pass 4, stage S5 of #19939 (stage plan `6096263424`, claim `6122880753`), under ruling D on #11182 and ADR-0032 Decisions 2 and 3. An `http` node reads each config key by what it is: `url` and every `headers` value are **text slots** with `{{ }}` holes (the plan's carry line), `body` is a **value slot** (a CEL value envelope or a literal), and `method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and `signingSecret` are **literals**, read as written (S4's seat order `6117306001`, answer B, applied per key on the census below). A single-brace `{…}` token at any of them is refused. The executor parses its config as authored, renders the request once before either mode, and no longer imports the single-brace interpolator. #19939 stays open for S6 and S7, so this PR says `Part of`.

## The census, per key (base `9432bac07`)

Every token-bearing string at an `http` node position, in `examples/**`, `content/docs/**` and `docs/**` (references and releases excluded), `packages/qa/dogfood`, `packages/platform-objects` and every tracked TS / JS file. The test column is the fix round's structural sweep at `1105b4a06` (each of the seven keys on an object typed `http`, ternary branches and helper arguments followed); the first census matched http fixtures by text and missed the ten strings marked †, rewritten in `af1317fd1`. hotcrm is not measured (another repository; the dispatch carries it).

| key | S5 | shipped (examples, docs, dogfood, platform-objects) | tests | why |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url` | text slot, `{{ }}` | 0 | 6: `lint-flow-credential-literals.test.ts:269` (a template draws no credential finding), `validate-flow-template-paths.test.ts:181`, `flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts:240`, `flow-text-slot-template.test.ts:259`, † `runtime-authoring-gate.flow-credential-literal.test.ts:39` and † `flow-credential-literal-doors.e2e.test.ts:71` (the DARK credential controls) | the plan's carry line (binding): a url is text |
| `headers.*` | text slot per value, `{{ }}`; a token written as the whole map refused | 0 | 5: `flow.test.ts:786` (`Bearer {$Credential.token}`), `flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts:224` (`headers: '{headers}'`, the build-door carve-out control), † `runtime-authoring-gate.flow-credential-literal.test.ts:42` and † `flow-credential-literal-doors.e2e.test.ts:74` (the DARK credential controls), † `lint-flow-credential-literals.test.ts:84` (the scanner's template control) | the plan's carry line (binding) |
| `body` | **value slot**, one value (the whole payload) | **5 tokens in 4 bodies**: showcase `flows/index.ts:1059` (text with a hole), `:1239` (two whole tokens), `:1444` (one); `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx:464` (one) | 5: † `flow.test.ts:492`-`:493` (the approval flow, two tokens), `flow.test.ts:788`, `flow-walk.test.ts:165`, `validate-flow-template-paths.test.ts:560`, † `validate-flow-template-paths.test.ts:465` (the hand-off helper, fed `:441`, `:490`, `:500`) | measured pull |
| `method` | **literal** (B) | 0 | 0 | no flow computes it |
| `durable` | **literal** (B) | 0 | 1: `flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts:223`, the build-door carve-out control | the one test pins the interpolation itself, not a use |
| `timeoutMs` | **literal** (B) | 0 | 2: `config-parse.test.ts:193` (the post-interpolation parse), `flow-builtin-node-config-values.test.ts:222` (the carve-out control) | both pin the interpolation itself |
| `signingSecret` | **literal** (B), run-resolved, ⛔ not a template or value slot | 0 | 5: `http-node-signing.test.ts:208`, `:241`, `:255`, `:309` (a secret through a template, and the "resolved to nothing" refusal), `guard-refusal-inventory.test.ts:160` | the tests pin the interpolation itself; the credential channel is unchanged |

**The test, applied.** A test that exists to pin the interpolation is not pull: it is the mechanism this card retires, the same reading S4's B gave the designer's picker ("a surface, not a use"). So the four zero-shipped keys are literals, and each such test is re-judged in this PR (below).

## FROM → TO, per position

| position | you wrote | write instead | what changes |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url` | `'https://api.example.com/v1/orders/{record.id}'` | `'https://api.example.com/v1/orders/{{ record.id }}'` | a `Date` renders as its ISO text, not JSON-quoted |
| `headers.X` | `'r-{record.id}'` | `'r-{{ record.id }}'` | a header that renders to no text is not sent (the template sent it empty) |
| `headers` (whole) | `'{headers}'` | the map: `{ 'X-Ref': '{{ record.id }}' }` | a map is not computed into it |
| `body` | `{ id: '{record.id}', status: 'done' }` | `{ dialect: 'cel', source: "{'id': record.id, 'status': dyn('done')}" }` | an absent `id` fails the run instead of sending `null`; a literal beside a field read is wrapped in `dyn(…)` (CEL holds a map's values to one type) |
| `body` | `{ text: 'Done: {record.title}' }` | `{ dialect: 'cel', source: "{'text': 'Done: ' + record.title}" }` | an absent `title` fails the run instead of sending `'Done: '` |
| `method` / `durable` / `timeoutMs` | `'{verb}'` / `'{flag}'` / `'{timeout}'` | the value itself: `'POST'` / `true` / `5000` | a literal now; nothing computes it |
| `signingSecret` | `'{signing_key}'` | the secret itself (a metadata-API save keeps it in the write-only credential store), or `''` | refused at the run |

**The one-line fix: double the braces in `url` and the `headers` values, write `body` as one CEL value envelope that builds the payload, and write `method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and `signingSecret` as the values themselves.**

## The mechanism assumptions, measured

- **A1 holds.** `HttpConfigSchema` (`io-node-config.zod.ts:745` at the base) carries `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body`, `durable`, `timeoutMs`, `signingSecret` and the `surface` / `history` keys of its `strictObject`, nothing else.
- **A2 holds, and what replaces the order.** `PARSED_AFTER_INTERPOLATION = new Set(['http'])` existed because `http-nodes.ts:182` parsed `interpolate(raw, …)`: the build doors judged an `http` rule only on a config carrying no token at all. The executor no longer interpolates, so the set had one member and loses it; the constant and its one line in `builtinValueJudged` are deleted (a set that is always empty is a check that can never fire). What replaces the order: credential channel → parse the config **as authored** → render `url` and the `headers` values → evaluate `body` → either mode. That is the order every other contract-carrying builtin already had (notify since S4).
- **A3 holds, with one note.** `http-nodes.ts` imports `renderTextSlot` and `resolveValueSlot`, not `interpolate`. A literal body passes through `resolveValueSlot`'s residual `interpolate()` (the identity on a token-free literal; the contract parse refused any token first), the same residual call S1–S4's slots make, which S7 deletes. The three `??` left in the executor are the declared absent-key defaults, not tolerance of an off-spec shape: `cfg.method ?? 'POST'` / `?? 'GET'` (the contract documents both, and why there is no `.default()`), and `payload: body ?? {}` on the outbox arm (unchanged).
- **A4 holds, and the request is rendered once.** At the base the whole config was interpolated in the executor before the durable branch, and `service-messaging`'s outbox and dispatcher render nothing (`http-outbox.ts` stores the url, headers and payload as handed; read at the base). After S5 the executor renders `url` and the headers and evaluates `body` once, before the durable / inline branch, so the outbox enqueues exactly what the inline call would send — pinned (`http-slots.test.ts` 3: the enqueued url, headers and payload are the rendered ones, and nothing in the enqueue carries a `{{`).

## `signingSecret` — the one judgement this PR settles itself

The binding text: "`signingSecret` is a run-resolved key (`RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS`): its secret-reference resolution stays exactly as it is. ⛔ Do not turn it into a template or value slot." Read with A2 ("once no `{var}` is read at any `http` key") and A3 ("no longer calls `interpolate`"), the resolution that stays is the write-only credential channel, and it does: `holdsFlowCredential` / `resolveFlowCredential` and `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` are byte-identical. What goes is the `{token}` interpolation of the secret, which the census shows only the interpolation's own tests ever wrote. The key is therefore a literal (S4's B), a token in it is refused with a remedy that never echoes the value, and because the build doors leave a run-resolved key to the run, that refusal is the executor's parse — pinned both ways (`registerFlow` and `objectstack validate` accept `signingSecret: '{k}'`; the run refuses it, nothing is sent). The dead "set but resolved to no value" refusal goes with the interpolation: with nothing rendered, the parsed secret is the authored one. Four axes: no measured business use (tests only); one dialect and S7's resolver deletion stay possible (keeping `interpolate` on this one key would block it); a token is refused loudly at the run instead of signing with its braces or leaving unsigned; immediate retirement, no window. The boundary this leaves is in Acceptance notes.

## What lands

**The contract (`@objectstack/spec`).**
- `url` stays `z.string()` and each `headers` value `z.string()`; the contract's refinement refuses a single-brace token in either through the one text-slot judge (`textSlotTemplateRefusal`), with its hole spelling, and a hole over a `$` root the engine does not bind.
- `body` takes `FlowValueSlotSchema`: an object naming a `dialect` must be a valid CEL value envelope, and a `{…}` token in any string of a literal is refused by the one value-slot judge, which names the envelope that builds the whole body.
- `method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and `signingSecret` keep their 17.x types; a token or an envelope there is refused with the literal's remedy. The refusal of a token at `method`, `durable`, `timeoutMs` and of a token written as the whole `headers` map carries `READ_AS_WRITTEN_PARAM` (S4's mechanism, unchanged), so the build doors report it. The refinement runs with `when: () => true`, so a token at a typed literal (`timeoutMs: '{t}'`) gets the literal's sentence beside the type's refusal; the build doors report the marked one, once.
- Every `describe()` of the http keys is restated, and the module docblock.

**The ledger and the doors.**
- `FLOW_NODE_EXPRESSION_PATHS` appends the `http` `body` row (one value, the whole payload); every older row is byte-identical (pinned).
- `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` gains `http.url` and `http.headers`. The exported `FlowNodeTextSlot` gains the optional `eachValue`: `flowNodeTextSlotSources` yields each value of the map at its own path (`headers.X-Ref`), so `registerFlow` and `objectstack validate` judge and compile each header like every other text slot.
- `HttpConfigSchema` joins `LEDGER_DECLARED_NODE_CONFIG_SCHEMAS`, which carries the body's `xExpression: 'value'` to the reconciliation ratchet (the descriptor offers `body` with no marker: one slot, one channel).
- `flow-node-config-refusals.ts`: `PARSED_AFTER_INTERPOLATION` and its line are deleted (A2); `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS` is unchanged.

**The executor (`@objectstack/service-automation`).** `http-nodes.ts` parses the config as authored (after the credential channel), renders `url` and each header through `renderTextSlot` (a url that renders to no text refuses the node, a header that renders to no text is not sent), evaluates `body` through the shared `resolveValueSlot`, reads the literals as written, and no longer imports `interpolate`. The descriptor's help strings are restated; its `type`s are unchanged.

**The lint (`@objectstack/lint`, patch).** The notify-literal hint machinery becomes per node type (`LITERAL_KEYS` / `LITERAL_HINTS`): at an `http` literal both wrong-syntax hints say that neither brace dialect resolves there and name the value itself. The `flow-double-brace-interpolation` hints name the http url and headers among the text slots. The credential-literal docblock stops calling `http`'s single brace its template. `objectstack validate` refuses each position through the shared judges and the contract, with no rule change.

**ADR-0087, D3 only.** `18.flow-value-slot-template-dialect-refused` (surface: the http body and its four literals; replacement, reason, acceptance), `18.flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused` and `18.flow-text-slot-unbound-dollar-root-refused` (surface: the http url and headers values), and `18.flow-builtin-node-config-values-refused` with its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment (it said `http` parses after interpolating and that only an `http` typed slot may take a sole-token template; both stop being true here). No D2: an absent value in the body wrote `null` or nothing under the template and fails the run under CEL; a whole token at `timeoutMs` / `durable` resolved to its type and is text now; a `Date` in a url or header rendered JSON-quoted under the interpolator and as ISO text under the engine. No key is removed, so no tombstone. The changeset marker is `not-required (already-registered …)` naming the four ids.

**Sites.** The showcase's three bodies (`flows/index.ts`) and the flows guide's http example are migrated; a literal beside a field read inside a CEL map literal is wrapped in `dyn(…)` (measured: `{'id': record.id, 'status': 'done'}` is refused by the CEL checker at `registerFlow`, "Map value uses wrong type"). The flows guide gains an http paragraph and the http keys in its text-slot and value-slot lists and its dialect table; the service-automation README's dialect table likewise. Test fixtures that wrote the retired spellings at these keys are re-judged: in the first pass `flow.test.ts`'s api flow, the lint credential-literal fixtures, `config-parse.test.ts`, the signing tests, the guard-refusal inventory and the build-door carve-out control; in the fix round (`af1317fd1`) every remaining fixture the structural sweep found outside the refusal pins: the two DARK credential controls (`metadata-protocol` save door, `cli` doors; `{{ api_token }}` at the url and header, still no advisory), the lint scanner's template header control (`{{ run_token }}`), `flow-walk.test.ts`'s body (a CEL envelope), `validate-flow-template-paths.test.ts`'s url pin (a `{{ }}` hole) and hand-off payload (moved from the body, which no template reaches, to an `X-Billing-Amount` header text slot), and `flow.test.ts`'s approval-flow body (a CEL envelope, now parsed against `HttpConfigSchema`).

## Pins, and the ablations that turn them red

- `http-slots.test.ts` (service-automation, 21 engine pins): each position refused at `registerFlow`, located and in its own judge's words; the executor's contract parse refuses url, header and body tokens and each literal's token as a guard, nothing sent; `signingSecret` accepted at `registerFlow` and refused at the run; holes render in the url and headers, the body envelope evaluates (`dyn`), a literal body and a nested envelope are sent as written, a whole hole holding a map renders JSON; the durable enqueue carries the rendered request; a url rendering nothing refuses the node, a header rendering nothing is not sent, an absent variable in the body fails the run with `EXECUTION_ERROR` naming `body`.

- service-automation: `config-expression-ledger.test.ts` (http declares its one value slot on the spec Zod channel alone); `config-parse.test.ts`, `http-node-signing.test.ts`, `guard-refusal-inventory.test.ts` re-judged.
- lint: `validate-expressions.test.ts` (`objectstack validate` refuses each position; `signingSecret` left to the run); `lint-flow-patterns.test.ts` (the http literal hints, the contract's literal keys asked of the contract; the #16405 controls move to a CRUD `filter`, the one position S6 has not reached).

## Acceptance notes

- **`signingSecret` is refused at the run, not at the build doors** — the binding run-resolved order. So a Studio save of `signingSecret: '{k}'` is accepted, moves into the credential store, and every run of that node is refused (as a guard, nothing sent, the remedy naming the secret itself). Making it a build-door refusal would mean reading the marked token refusal ahead of `RUN_RESOLVED_KEYS`, which would also refuse a packaged flow whose credential-store row supplies the secret the run actually signs with; that is a contract decision for the seat, not taken here.
- **A body envelope that evaluates to `null`** sends no body inline and `{}` to the outbox (`payload: body ?? {}`) — the same asymmetry an absent body had before; unchanged.
- **A CEL map literal holds one value type.** `{'id': record.id, 'status': 'done'}` is refused at `registerFlow` by the CEL checker ("Map value uses wrong type, expected type 'dyn' but found 'string'"), loud, and the value-slot judge's own remedy names `dyn(…)`; the docs, the describe, the changeset and the examples write the `dyn` form.
- `validate-flow-template-paths` still path-checks a single-brace `{record.x}` in an http body, beside the value-slot judge's refusal of the same token; its single-brace reading goes in S7.
- The lint's http literal keys are a local set, as S4's notify set is; a pin asks the contract which keys refuse a token as read-as-written and holds the set to it (the contract also lists `headers`, whose whole-map token it refuses; its values are text slots, where `{{ }}` is the spelling).
- **NOT MEASURED:** `pnpm check:type-check-debt` (the dispatch rules it out: `--re-measure` plus an unlocked whole-workspace build) and `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (it loads every published `require` entry, so it needs the whole workspace's `dist`; CI's); hotcrm at these keys (another repository; the dispatch carries it).
- **Carried by the seat, not here:** the skill text (`skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:236`–`:241` lists `http` among the slots that keep the single brace) to #22585; the objectui designer's `http` pickers to an objectui companion card.
